title: pvAxisAlignedSlice
body:
## pvAxisAlignedSlice

Slices hyper tree grids and overlapping AMR data with an axis-aligned plane while keeping the input type, so a 3-D hyper tree grid becomes 2-D hyper tree grids. For hyper tree grids each entry of OffsetValues gives one slice and the output is a partitioned dataset collection; for AMR one slice at the plane is produced, at resolution Level. Use slice or pvSlice for ordinary meshes.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Only vtkHyperTreeGrid and vtkOverlappingAMR inputs are accepted.
- The cut plane must be axis-aligned; oblique normals are not supported.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `AxisAlignedSlice`. Identity: `filters/AxisAlignedSlice`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input of the slice filter. Accepted data: hyper-tree grids (adaptive AMR-like trees) (vtkHyperTreeGrid); overlapping AMR data (vtkOverlappingAMR). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkHyperTreeGrid","vtkOverlappingAMR"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CutFunction` | This property sets the parameters of the cut function. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Axis Aligned Plane"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Axis Aligned Plane"}` |
| `Level` | Set maximum slice resolution. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `OffsetValues` | The values in this property specify a list of current slice offset values. This can be used to create multiple slices with different centers. Each entry represents a new slice with its center shifted by the offset value. The 'Values Range' information is the range based on the global bounding box, not necessarily on the current slice geometry configuration. **These offset values are added to the global offset value set through the "Offset" property.** | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1]` |

### Nested `CutFunction` → `Axis Aligned Plane`

Syntax: `{"type":"Axis Aligned Plane","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Axis Aligned Plane`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CutFunction.options.AlwaysSnapToNearestAxis` | When true, ParaView replaces Normal by the coordinate axis of its largest absolute component, so the plane is always perpendicular to x, y or z. The snapped normal is always positive ([-1, 0, 0] becomes [1, 0, 0]), and tied components are all set to 1 ([1, 1, 0] stays [1, 1, 0]) rather than resolved to one axis. When false, Normal is used as given. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `CutFunction.options.Normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `CutFunction.options.Offset` | Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `CutFunction.options.Origin` | A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvAxisAlignedSlice",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
